subject.title: fix: prevent operational notices from leaking to source chats

question: After fixing redirect failure and conflicts, should OpenClaw ship the full four-mode operational-notice policy, including durable once-state and cross-session redirect?
rationale: The branch addresses a real leakage problem but creates new public config, persistent state, plugin API, failure-mode, and sensitive cross-session routing contracts that implementation correctness alone cannot approve.

options.title: Approve after repair
options.body: Keep all four modes after preserving notices on redirect failure, defining target authorization, resolving conflicts, and proving fresh-install and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Narrow to suppression
options.body: Fix source-chat leakage through the existing delivery boundary and defer redirect, durable once-state, and plugin API expansion.

options.title: Defer the policy
options.body: Pause the PR until operational-notice classification and routing are defined as a separate product contract.

recommendation.title: Approve after repair
recommendation.body: Keep all four modes after preserving notices on redirect failure, defining target authorization, resolving conflicts, and proving fresh-install and upgrade behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history signal spans both core reply dispatch and transcript persistence, the main architectural and product-decision boundaries in this PR.
